objective: Examine how monthly option premium decay and expiry-time behaviour should be modeled as a market-context intelligence feature
note: No files were modified for this task. All findings below were verified by reading server.ts directly (grep + line-by-line inspection), not recalled from memory.

current_implementation_findings.requirement: How monthly option premiums are currently recorded/calculated
current_implementation_findings.verified: PremiumData (server.ts line 29) stores strike, isAtm, bid/ask, lastPrice, change, iv, oi, volume, vwap(+honesty flag), quoteTimestamp, atDayHigh/atDayLow, dayHigh/dayLow, pdc (previous day close), pdh/pdl (previous day high/low FOR THIS OPTION'S PREMIUM), and vega/theta/delta.
current_implementation_findings.correction_to_task_framing: Contrary to an older project decision (recorded 2026-07-25) to skip Greeks as 'too complex,' Greeks WERE later implemented. calcImpliedVolatility() (bisection method solving for IV from market price) and calcGreeks() (full Black-Scholes vega/delta/theta) both exist and are actively called for ATM CE/PE. This is a correction to prior assumptions, not new work.

current_implementation_findings.requirement: Whether the system tracks premium from an initial reference (e.g. ₹900/₹700) and computes absolute/percentage loss
current_implementation_findings.verified: NOT PRESENT. pdh/pdl track the PREVIOUS TRADING DAY's high/low for that strike's premium (one-day lookback), not a decay-from-entry tracker. The only 'entry reference' concept anywhere in the codebase is the Rule Engine's suggested trade (Entry/SL/T1/T2, percentage-of-premium formula, built 2026-08-08) and the new Validation/Outcome Engine that evaluates THAT specific suggestion against SL/T1/T2 — neither is a general-purpose 'track this contract's decay since day 1 of the month' feature.

current_implementation_findings.requirement: How remaining time to monthly expiry is represented
current_implementation_findings.verified: daysToExpiry = (expiry.expiryDate.getTime() - Date.now()) / 86_400_000 (lines 2576, 2614) — a raw millisecond difference converted to days. This is CALENDAR time, fed directly into the Black-Scholes T = daysToExpiry/365 term.

current_implementation_findings.requirement: Calendar days vs actual trading days to expiry
current_implementation_findings.verified: NOT DISTINGUISHED. Only calendar-day arithmetic exists; there is no trading-day-count function anywhere in the codebase.

current_implementation_findings.requirement: Final 1–2 weeks acceleration effect / can the system detect accelerating decay
current_implementation_findings.verified: NOT PRESENT. theta is computed as an instantaneous Black-Scholes snapshot (today's rate), not tracked over time, so there is no mechanism to observe or flag that decay is accelerating as expiry nears. The Black-Scholes formula itself mathematically implies faster time-decay as T→0, but nothing in the code surfaces this as a signal, alert, or trend.

current_implementation_findings.requirement: Market holidays / non-trading days before expiry
current_implementation_findings.verified: NOT IMPLEMENTED. GET /api/holidays (line 10997) is a hardcoded stub: `return c.json([]);` — it always returns an empty array. The Holidays tab UI exists (renderHolidays) but has no real data source. This means no holiday-awareness exists anywhere, which is also why trading-day-vs-calendar-day cannot currently be computed — there is no holiday list to subtract.

current_implementation_findings.requirement: Separating decay into intrinsic value, extrinsic/time value, IV changes, and underlying price movement
current_implementation_findings.verified: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED, NOT ASSEMBLED. iv (via calcImpliedVolatility) and vega/theta/delta (via calcGreeks) ARE computed per ATM leg. But: (a) intrinsic value is NEVER computed anywhere — the word 'intrinsic' does not appear in the codebase at all; (b) there is no function that decomposes a premium CHANGE into 'this much was intrinsic (spot movement), this much was time decay, this much was an IV shift' — each Greek exists as an independent snapshot number, not combined into an attribution/decomposition.

current_implementation_findings.requirement: ITM/ATM/OTM status and its effect on remaining value — do not assume expiry value is always zero
current_implementation_findings.verified: Only isAtm: boolean exists on PremiumData. There is no isItm/isOtm flag or classification function. ITM/OTM status is not pre-computed anywhere; it would need to be derived ad hoc by comparing strike vs spot at read time. No code anywhere asserts or assumes a monthly option goes to zero — but nothing currently models what an ITM contract's terminal (expiry) value should be either (i.e. intrinsic value at expiry), since intrinsic value isn't computed at all (see above).

computeGapScore() (line 2180) already classifies each day into Continuation / Fade Risk / Sideways (GapScore interface, line 63), combining gap direction, VWAP position, PDH/PDL status, OI tilt, and sector breadth. This is the closest existing 'market regime' concept in the codebase. There is no explicit reversal-vs-continuation-over-multiple-days classifier, and no volatility-regime (high-IV vs low-IV environment) classifier beyond the raw india_vix level already used as a rule-engine signal.

existing_modules_functions_data_fields_i: PremiumData interface (server.ts ~line 29) — per-strike data, including iv/vega/theta/delta
pdh/pdl/pdc fields on PremiumData — previous-day levels for THIS strike's premium (1-day lookback, not month-long tracking)
computeGapScore() / GapScore interface (~lines 63, 2180) — existing market-context classifier (Continuation/Fade Risk/Sideways)
Rule Engine's suggestion block (runRuleEngine, built 2026-08-08) — Entry/SL/T1/T2 percentage formula, the closest existing 'reference value' concept

Validation/Outcome Engine (outcome-engine.ts, built 2026-08-08/09) — evaluates a SPECIFIC suggested trade against SL/T1/T2 within a configurable window; architecturally the closest existing pattern for 'track value over time from a reference point', though scoped to the Rule Engine's own suggestions, not general monthly-contract decay
renderAtmDetailCard or equivalent (~lines 7456–7466) — the only place Greeks are currently displayed (ATM CE/PE, instantaneous values, no history)
what_is_already_supported: IV computation (implied, solved from market price)
Full Black-Scholes vega/theta/delta for ATM CE/PE (instantaneous snapshot)
Previous-day (1-day) high/low/close for any strike's premium
A market-context/gap classifier (Continuation/Fade Risk/Sideways) that a decay feature could plug into
A percentage-of-premium reference-and-target pattern (Rule Engine's SL/T1/T2), architecturally reusable as a template
A 'measure something against a reference over a time window, exclude incomplete data' pattern (Validation/Outcome Engine), architecturally reusable as a template
what_is_missing: Any tracking of a contract's premium against an INITIAL/entry reference value over the life of the contract (only 1-day PDH/PDL exists, not month-long)
Trading-day-aware time-to-expiry (only calendar days exist; T=daysToExpiry/365 feeds Black-Scholes with calendar time)
A real holiday list (the endpoint is a stub returning [])
Any decay-acceleration detection or alert (theta is a snapshot, not a trend)
Intrinsic value computation (does not exist anywhere in the codebase)
A decomposition of a premium change into intrinsic-move vs time-decay vs IV-shift components
An explicit ITM/OTM classification flag (only isAtm exists)
Any explicit link between decay rate/pattern and the existing Gap/market-context classifier — they are currently two unconnected concepts

recommended_architecture.fits_existing_layer: Feature Extraction (System Architecture v1.0, layer 4) for the deterministic calculations (intrinsic/extrinsic split, trading-days-to-expiry, decay-rate-vs-reference); Indicator/Signal Engine (layer 5) IF a decay-based signal is wanted for the rule engine's score; a NEW lightweight 'Premium Behaviour' read-model for the reference-tracking/percentage-loss/decay-acceleration view, since nothing existing does that job.
recommended_architecture.new_engine_vs_extension: Recommend an EXTENSION, not a new top-level engine. The pieces needed (intrinsic-value calc, trading-day count, decay-rate-vs-reference) are Feature Extraction-level calculations that belong alongside the existing Greeks computation, not a standalone 'engine' with its own architectural layer. A genuinely new engine would only be justified if this needed its own scoring/verdict/decision logic separate from the Rule Engine — nothing examined here requires that.
recommended_architecture.reuse_over_new_module: Two existing patterns are directly reusable rather than reinvented: (1) the Rule Engine's percentage-of-premium reference pattern (Entry/SL/T1/T2) generalizes naturally to 'track % change from a chosen reference premium'; (2) the Outcome Engine's window-based tracking-with-honest-incompleteness pattern generalizes to 'track a contract's value over the remaining life of the month, marking gaps/incompleteness explicitly rather than interpolating.'

recommended_deterministic_calculations: Intrinsic value: max(spot − strike, 0) for CE, max(strike − spot, 0) for PE — currently entirely missing, cheapest and highest-value addition.
Extrinsic/time value: premium − intrinsic value — trivial once intrinsic exists.

Trading-days-to-expiry: requires a REAL holiday list first (the current /api/holidays stub must be filled with actual NSE holiday dates — this is a prerequisite, not optional, since 'distinguish calendar from trading days' is impossible without it).

Decay-rate-vs-reference: % change = (currentPremium − referencePremium) / referencePremium, where referencePremium is either a user-chosen entry point or, for a general 'monthly behaviour' view, the first recorded premium after the monthly contract became the front-month/current contract.

Decay-acceleration flag: compare today's per-day extrinsic-value change to the trailing N-day average — deterministic, no new external data needed, but needs several days of history to be meaningful (same 'don't fabricate confidence on too little data' principle already established for the Outcome Engine's MIN_SAMPLE_SIZE).
recommended_market_context_relationships: Reuse computeGapScore()'s existing Continuation/Fade Risk/Sideways label as the market-context tag attached to each day's decay reading — do not build a second, competing classifier.

Relate decay rate to IV level/trend (already computed via calcImpliedVolatility) — e.g. 'time value eroding while IV also falling' vs 'time value eroding while IV rising' are different, useful distinctions, and the raw ingredients already exist.

Do NOT build a new 'trending/reversal' multi-day classifier for this feature specifically — that would duplicate the Market Regime Engine already deferred in docs/architecture.md pending real Outcome Engine data; reuse or wait for that instead of a parallel one-off.

how_haiku_should_consume_this.principle: Same boundary already established for the Rule Engine (docs/architecture.md, section 6, AI Boundary): Haiku explains a decision, it does not compute one. This feature is entirely deterministic (intrinsic/extrinsic split, trading-day count, % change from reference, acceleration flag) — Haiku's only role would be to turn an already-computed structured result into a plain-language sentence, e.g. 'This contract has lost 42% of its value in 12 trading days, mostly from time decay rather than the underlying moving against it, and that decay is accelerating as expiry approaches.'
how_haiku_should_consume_this.structured_input_haiku_would_receive: verdict-style object: { referencePremium, currentPremium, pctChange, intrinsicValue, extrinsicValue, tradingDaysToExpiry, decayAccelerating: bool, marketContext: <existing GapScore verdict> } — the same pattern already used for the Rule Engine's Haiku call, extended with these new fields.
how_haiku_should_consume_this.hard_constraint: Haiku must never be allowed to state a premium's expected future value, a probability of expiring worthless, or a recommendation to hold/exit — those would cross from explanation into computation/advice, violating the same boundary already enforced elsewhere.

potential_risks_or_misleading_interpreta: Calendar-day Black-Scholes T already slightly OVERSTATES time value on the calculation side (since it includes non-trading days as if they contributed to decay uncertainty) — not a new risk from this feature, but worth knowing before layering a 'trading-day-aware' decay display on top of a calendar-day-based theta, since the two would use inconsistent time bases unless reconciled.

Presenting a raw % premium loss WITHOUT the intrinsic/extrinsic split would be actively misleading for an ITM contract — a large % move in TOTAL premium can be almost entirely intrinsic (i.e. just the underlying moving against the position), not decay at all. This is exactly the confusion the person's original question was probing, and is the strongest argument for building the intrinsic/extrinsic split before anything else in this list.
A 'decay acceleration' flag built on too few days of history would repeat the exact mistake already avoided in the Outcome Engine (MIN_SAMPLE_SIZE) — must not fire confidently on 2–3 days of data.

Holidays must be sourced from an authoritative NSE/BSE calendar, not hand-maintained, or the trading-day count will silently drift wrong across sessions/redeploys (same class of risk as the FII/DII manual-entry data, but higher-stakes since it feeds a time-value calculation directly).

None of this should be assumed to make Black-Scholes 'accurate' for Indian index options — the model's assumptions (constant volatility, European exercise — which does hold for NSE index options, log-normal returns) are simplifications; treating computed Greeks/IV as precise rather than model-estimated (as the code already honestly comments them) must be preserved, not eroded, by any new feature built on top.
implementation_plan_no_code_yet: Step 1 (prerequisite, blocking): populate GET /api/holidays with a real NSE/BSE trading holiday calendar. Nothing trading-day-aware can be built honestly before this.
Step 2: add intrinsic/extrinsic value computation (pure function, no new data source needed — uses existing spot + strike + premium).
Step 3: add a trading-days-to-expiry function using the Step 1 holiday list, alongside (not replacing) the existing calendar-day daysToExpiry used by Black-Scholes.

Step 4: add reference-premium tracking — needs a decision from the person on what 'reference' means (first day of the month? a user-chosen entry price? the Rule Engine's own suggested entry?) before this can be scoped further.
Step 5: add the decay-acceleration comparison, gated on a minimum history length (mirroring MIN_SAMPLE_SIZE's honesty principle).
Step 6: wire the existing GapScore verdict alongside the decay reading for market-context, and only then consider whether a Haiku explanation layer for this feature is wanted.
Each step should be its own reviewed, tested, deployed increment — not a single large change — consistent with how the Outcome Engine and every signal this session were built.
